title: Lateral Thinking Puzzles with LLMs
text:
puzzle.png



As discussed in class and in the book, These Strange New Minds, LLMs are truly powerful logical systems that have honed their abilities to solve logical puzzles, including those of lateral thinking puzzles. Lateral thinking puzzles are a genre of “word puzzles” that rely on outside-the-box thinking and rationalization to obtain context around a problem and answer the puzzle. I was curious in the LLM’s ability to accurately and swiftly deduce the answer. I decided to experiment the following lateral puzzle with gpt-4o and gemini 2.5 flash in the following prompt:

I have a lateral thinking puzzle for you. Try to solve it by asking one yes-or-no question at a time until you uncover the answer. Here’s the puzzle scenario:
A cabin is resting on the side of a mountain. It’s tightly sealed with all doors and windows locked from the inside. Strangely, everyone inside is dead, and they all met their demise at the same moment. There was no foul play—no murders, suicides, illnesses, or suffocation involved. Can you figure out how they died?

The trick behind this lateral thinking puzzle is that you need to think outside the box to find out that the “cabin” is not a cabin house as you would be led to believe because it is in the woods. It is actually an airplane cabin!
Now, let’s see how these LLMs do!

GPT-4o
GPT-4o was extremely efficient at answering the puzzle. It only took 3 questions for it to answer the puzzle. The three questions it asked included: > 1. Is the “cabin” a vehicle of some kind? > 2. Was the cabin an airplane? > 3. Did the airplane crash into the mountain, causing the deaths of everyone inside?
I asked the LLM after if it was familiar with the question, and it answered, “Yes, I’m familiar with this puzzle. It’s a classic lateral thinking puzzle that I’ve come across before.” Now, this leads me to believe that gpt-4o had already encountered this puzzle in its training data, so it was very well-equipped to answer this lateral thinking question.
I’m a little sad, as I felt that this didn’t feel like a full reflection of the LLM’s ability to reason and think through a problem, as it rather already had access to the solution. Nonetheless, it asked questions and arrived at a solution.


Gemini 2.5 Flash
Gemini 2.5 Flash took longer than I expected it to. While it seemed to make some headway quickly about the context of the problem, it had the assumption that the “cabin” was a stationary cabin in the mountain rather than a “cabin” in an aircraft for quite some time before it finally figured it out. In addition, this model appeared to take somewhat a more scientific approach in its response, asking about whether the cabin experienced a “rapid and significant change in altitude” or “experienced a sudden and catastrophic loss of internal pressure.” Thus, it took 8 questions in total to reach this conclusion, which is certainly impressive, but not as impressive as gpt-4o.
I felt that gemini 2.5 flash’s approach to the problem to be very unique as rather than understanding the accident as simply a plane crash, it tried to further rationalize the cause of death, attributing it to “rapid change in altitude” and pressure. I wonder if these differences in approach between gemini 2.5 flash and gpt-4o are due to unique differences in their training data and how they utilize their training data. Perhaps gemini 2.5 flash is used to giving more specific answers, and thus opted for this reasoning.



My Reflection
Overall, while it was interesting to experiment with the LLMs, the results didn’t quite come out the way I had hoped it would. It seems to me that the LLMs were much more familiar with the problems than I had originally hoped they would be, so they were able to get the answer much more quicker than I expected. Even so, I think it was interesting to see how each LLM approached the solution in different ways, where gemini 2.5 flash specifically took a unique approach of looking at the problem in context declining internal pressure rather than simply a plane crash.

title: Discovering New Recipes with LLMs
text:
Gemini_Generated_Image_md3rn5md3rn5md3r.png


As a HUGE foodie, I was curious to see what kinds of recipes LLMs could generate. More specifically, I’m interested to find out whether it can generate original recipes by combining other various recipes in its training data.
I used gpt-4o for this activity. I gave it the following prompt:

Create a completely original recipe that does not exist on the internet. This recipe should be unique in concept, flavor combination, and preparation method. Provide the following:

Image – Generate a realistic, appealing image of the finished dish.
Description – Write a detailed description of the dish, including: (1) the flavor profiles and textures, (2) the inspiration behind the recipe, and (3) what makes it original.
Recipe – Provide a complete recipe with: (1) a clear list of ingredients (with exact measurements), (2) step-by-step cooking instructions, and (3) tips or notes to enhance the dish.

Please give your recipe a name.


1. Citrus Grove Salmon Bowl





Description

Flavor Profiles & Textures: This dish brings together the richness of seared salmon with the unexpected brightness of citrus and nutty crunch. The salmon has a golden pistachio crust that’s slightly crisp on top, while the flesh remains buttery and flaky inside. It rests on a bed of short-grain rice that has been infused with a light citrus glaze, dotted with diced carrots and green peas for sweetness and freshness. Orange segments add a juicy burst of acidity, balancing the richness of the fish. Fresh basil provides a fragrant, herbal lift.
Inspiration: The inspiration came from the idea of combining three contrasting culinary traditions: the Mediterranean love for pistachios and herbs, Japanese-style rice bowls, and Southeast Asian citrus brightness. Instead of simply serving salmon with lemon, this dish incorporates whole orange segments, allowing the sweetness and acidity to mingle with savory rice and nutty pistachios.
What Makes It Original: Most citrus-salmon recipes focus on glazes or marinades. Here, the originality lies in layering citrus three ways: 1. In the rice (citrus glaze), 2. As garnish (fresh orange segments), and 3. Balanced with herbs and pistachios (creating a nutty-bright contrast).
The result is a dish that feels familiar yet truly novel, with each bite offering a shifting balance of savory, nutty, sweet, and tangy.


Ingredients (Serves 2)

For the salmon:
2 salmon fillets, skin removed (about 6 oz / 170 g each)
2 tbsp olive oil
2 tbsp unsalted pistachios, finely chopped
2 tbsp panko breadcrumbs
1 tsp honey
½ tsp smoked paprika
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper
For the citrus rice:
1 cup short-grain rice, rinsed
1 ¾ cups water
½ tsp salt
1 tbsp olive oil
½ cup diced carrot
½ cup green peas (fresh or frozen)
2 tbsp fresh orange juice
1 tsp soy sauce
For garnish:
1 large orange, peeled and segmented
2 tbsp chopped pistachios
Fresh basil leaves


Instructions


Prepare the rice:


Rinse the rice until water runs clear. Combine with water and salt in a small pot, bring to a boil, then reduce to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a pan. Sauté diced carrots for 3–4 minutes until slightly tender, then add peas and cook 2 more minutes.
Once rice is cooked, fluff with a fork and fold in the sautéed vegetables, orange juice, and soy sauce. Set aside.


Prepare the salmon crust:


In a bowl, mix chopped pistachios, panko, honey, paprika, salt, and pepper until crumbly.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Press the pistachio mixture firmly on the top of each fillet.


Cook the salmon:


Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Place salmon crust-side down first for 2 minutes to lightly crisp the crust, then carefully flip.
Cook the second side for 4–5 minutes until salmon is golden and just cooked through.


Assemble the dish:


Spoon the citrus rice into bowls. Place a salmon fillet on top.
Garnish with orange segments, a sprinkle of chopped pistachios, and fresh basil leaves.



Tips & Notes

Texture Balance: Don’t skip the quick crisping of the pistachio crust—it creates a caramelized, nutty layer that contrasts with the salmon’s tenderness.
Citrus Variety: Blood oranges or mandarins work beautifully for seasonal variations.
Make It a Meal: Serve with a simple side salad of greens tossed in a light vinaigrette to round out the citrus-herbal theme.
Rice Alternative: Quinoa or farro can replace short-grain rice if you prefer a heartier base.

2. Velvet Halibut





Description

Flavor Profiles & Textures: This dish layers bold contrasts: a pan-seared block of fish (mild and buttery, with a crisp golden crust) sits atop a smooth, roasted carrot–miso purée, which adds sweet depth and savory umami. On top, a warm relish of sautéed red peppers, green onions, and toasted walnuts provides a bright, nutty crunch that cuts through the richness of the fish. The final balance is a play of silky purée, crunchy garnish, tender fish, and a citrusy glaze that ties it all together.
Inspiration Behind the Recipe: The idea came from blending two culinary traditions — the smooth earthiness of root-vegetable purées from classic French cuisine with the miso-based balance of Japanese cooking. Adding a nut-and-vegetable relish on top makes it interactive, bringing texture and color to every bite.
What Makes It Original: 1. Carrot–miso purée (instead of the more common potato or cauliflower base). 2. A warm walnut–pepper relish as a “sauce” substitute, offering crunch instead of liquid. 3. The layering concept: bottom (creamy), middle (meaty fish), top (crisp relish). This creates a three-tier sensory experience in a single forkful.


Ingredients (Serves 2)

For the carrot–miso purée:
3 medium carrots, peeled and chopped (about 250 g)
1 tbsp white miso paste
2 tbsp unsalted butter
½ cup vegetable broth
½ tsp lemon zest
Pinch of salt
For the fish:
2 thick fillets of halibut, cod, or sea bass (about 6 oz / 170 g each)
1 tbsp olive oil
Salt and pepper to taste
For the walnut–pepper relish:
½ cup red bell pepper, julienned
2 green onions, sliced thin
¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
1 tbsp olive oil
1 tsp apple cider vinegar
½ tsp honey
Pinch of salt
Finishing glaze (optional but recommended):
1 tbsp fresh orange juice
1 tsp soy sauce
½ tsp honey


Instructions


Make the carrot–miso purée:


In a small saucepan, add carrots and vegetable broth. Simmer until very tender (12–15 minutes).
Blend carrots with miso paste, butter, and lemon zest until silky. Season lightly with salt. Keep warm.


Cook the fish:


Pat fillets dry, season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high.
Sear fish 3–4 minutes per side until golden crust forms and flesh is just cooked through. Remove and rest.


Prepare the walnut–pepper relish:


Heat olive oil in a pan over medium. Add red pepper, cook 3–4 minutes until softened but still vibrant.
Stir in green onions, walnuts, vinegar, honey, and salt. Toss briefly and remove from heat.


Optional glaze:


In the same pan, deglaze with orange juice, soy sauce, and honey. Reduce slightly until glossy.


Assemble:


Spread carrot–miso purée as a base on each plate.
Place fish fillet on top.
Spoon walnut–pepper relish generously over fish.
Drizzle with glaze for brightness.



Tips & Notes

Fish choice: Firm white fish works best (halibut, cod, or sea bass). Salmon is also an option for a richer variation.
Purée consistency: Add more broth if you prefer a looser base.
Relish variations: Try hazelnuts or almonds instead of walnuts for different flavor notes.
Make-ahead: Carrot–miso purée can be prepared up to 2 days in advance.

Reflection
Overall, I was a little stunned by these two recipes. While I suppose they are original, they are certainly interesting in not the best possible light. It’s like something a broke college kid might throw together at 2 a.m., then somehow plated like it belongs in a Michelin-star restaurant. The contrast is both impressive and a little confusing. Part of me is curious to see if the flavors actually work in real life, because perhaps there’s some hidden genius in the chaos that is this recipe. It may even be possible that gpt-4o drew from recipes that included these flavor profiles. But really? Orange juice, soy sauce, and honey? Maybe it’s just me and I haven’t tried this end of the flavor pyramid, but it does sound a little far-fetched.
Perhaps one of these days I’ll give one of these recipes a shot in the kitchen to truly put AI to the test, but for now, I think I might keep this one away from the frying pan.

Given these three points, please write an image prompt that would consolidate these three points and create a visual depiction of the music.


GPT-5
I was thoroughly impressed by GPT-5’s analysis of the piece. It particularly commented on the exhilarating nature of the piece and the excitement it invokes in its listeners. It also comments on how the music makes you feel both “tension and release,” which then ultimately has the effect of making “you feel lifted, [carried, and transformed].”
Ultimately, GPT-5 gave me the following image prompt, which then generated the images (Gemini & GPT-5):

A dynamic, heroic scene: a tall winged figure (angelic or Valkyrie‐like) soaring high above a dramatic, storm-scoured mountain valley. Massive brass-coloured wings span wide, catching the slanting light of a breaking dawn. Below, rugged peaks and dark clouds part to reveal golden rays and swirling mist. The figure is clad in flowing armor that reflects both classical and mythic motifs, the pose one of triumphant ascent: wings fully spread, one fist raised, head tilted up toward the light. The palette: deep storm blues and grays in the lower valley, transitioning to warm golds, amber and white light above. In the background, the remnants of battle: broken spears, ancient stone, scattered banners but these are partially obscured by lifting mist. The composition: sweeping diagonals that convey movement and lift, the wings and light forming a V-shape which echoes triumph. The mood: epic, liberating, powerful, mythic. High detail, cinematic lighting, painterly style with a hint of modern digital clarity — suitable for an epic fantasy poster.

Image 1: Gemini:  Image 2: GPT-5: 


Gemini
Gemini also gave an equally thoughtful response and analysis of this piece. It was also able to comment on the “epic power, relentless urgency, and exhilarating grandeur” that the music creates. Notably, I thought that it was interesting that Gemini included time stamps of specific parts of the piece. I’ll include them below: > - “The Driving Rhythm [00:00:00 - 00:00:28]: The piece begins with a hypnotic, pulsating figure in the cellos and basses, creating a foundation of tension and relentless forward motion, like the beating of enormous wings or the churning of a great engine. > - The Iconic Brass Motif [00:58]: The moment the French horns and trumpets introduce the soaring, unforgettable main theme, it immediately feels like a triumphant battle-cry. This rising and falling figure in the brass creates a visual sense of flight and soaring through the air. > - The Orchestral Climax [01:28]: The shift to the full, booming fortissimo (very loud) sound of the entire orchestra—with heavy percussion, full brass, and sweeping strings—is a breathtaking surge of energy. This massive sound stands out as a declaration of pure, unstoppable force.”
Ultimately, Gemini gave me the following image prompt, which then generated the following images (Gemini & GPT-5):

An epic, hyper-detailed digital painting, highly cinematic, showing a squadron of eight Valkyries in gleaming, battle-worn silver and bronze armor. They are mounted on powerful, winged horses, charging relentlessly through a turbulent, deep indigo and crimson-streaked storm sky. The composition must emphasize dramatic forward motion and speed. Lightning strikes illuminate the scene, casting stark highlights on the brass of their musical instruments and the metallic gleam of their armor. The atmosphere is martial, chaotic, and supremely majestic. Inspired by Richard Wagner’s ’Ride of The Valkyries.

Image 1: Gemini:  Image 2: GPT-5: 




Conclusion
This was such a fascinating activity and likely one of my most favorite blog posts I’ve written thus far! When comparing between the LLM’s generations and refleciton of the music compared to mine, it feels as though their analyses are more “correct” as it likely draws from databases analysing this piece. Due to this, I do wonder how much of this output is a generalization of analysis of this musical piece completed by musicians prior, or the LLM’s own independent generalization and analysis of the musical orchestration and patterns in this piece. The similar motifs and reflections generated by both Gemini and GPT-5 hints to me that it is likely the former, but it would be exciting to dive into this topic more deeply and learn more about LLM competency in the use of music theory.

title: Real Vs. Fake: The Rise of Sora AI
text:
sora.png



In today’s digital age, the line between reality and fabrication is becoming increasingly blurred, thanks to the rapid advancements AI-generated videos. These videos are widespread, encompassing a wide range of content—from soothing ASMR clips and entertaining animal antics to more sinister applications that include spreading misinformation and creating lifelike videos of political figures. In this blog, I wanted to survey my friends and see whether they would believe my AI video was real.

For this purpose, I used Video AI by invideo, powered by sora AI, which has been taking the general media by storm. I wanted to generate a video that seemed the most innoncent of all–an adorable animal video. I generated it in the form of a tiktok so that it would seem more realistic to my friends.
This was the conversation I had: > Me: Create a realistic tiktok video featuring a dog and cat playing with each other. > > Assistant: Here are two ideas to choose from: > - Option A – “Best Buddies Forever” (30 sec) A warm, cozy, heart-melting short showing a dog and cat playing together in slow motion — light background music, golden lighting, and a cheerful narration about unlikely friendships. > > - Option B – “Battle of the Furballs” (45 sec) Funny, fast-paced, and meme-style — zooms, playful music, and captions as if the dog and cat are having a mock battle, ending in a cuddle. > Me: A, as long as its giving wholesome and fuzzy heart-warming vibes. No narration is needed. > > Assistant: Just to confirm before I generate it: > * Platform: TikTok > * Style: Realistic, cozy, natural lighting, no narration (just music & visuals) > * Duration: ~30 seconds > * Mood: Wholesome, warm, “aww” vibes — dog and cat playing affectionately indoors or in a sunlit garden > > Me: Keep it natural with ambient sounds
Would you like me to include soft background music (like acoustic or piano), or leave it completely natural with ambient sounds (like their playful barks/meows)?
Which one do you prefer, or do you have another tone in mind (e.g., cinematic, ASMR, funny, cute, emotional)?
The video is embedded below:

%%html
<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/shorts/yccjHob05u8" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen></iframe>




If not showing above, the link is available here: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/yccjHob05u8
Then, I shared this video with 7 of my friends and asked them if they thought it was AI while we were sharing tiktok videos together. I worded it in the way below to make the question appear less suspicious: > “Wait is this real or is this AI?”

Survey Results & Reflection
Overall, all 7 of my friends were able to guess that the video was AI-generated. Many of them pointed out that the “video looked fake” because of the textures in the video. Despite being able to accurately identify that it was an AI video, many of them had also exclaimed on the realism of the video and how great the quality was.
If my friends had been any less keen on technology, I think it would have been easy to fool someone into thinking that this was a real video with real animals. Even more, if technology continues to improve at this rapid rate, it’s possible that humans are no longer able to distinguish between AI and real videos anymore.
One thing I also wonder that I hope to investigate more in the future is what source and training materials LLMs use to generate these videos. I’d be curious learn more about how this source material influences the type of product generated.

title: These Strange New Minds: Introduction to NLPs
text:
miff.png




Reflection
Chapter 7 begins by dissecting this idea of language acquisition and how natural language processing (NLP) researchers are able to encode human language. Summerfield then introduces the idea of apes learning sign language in chapter 8. Nim was a chimpanzee who was taught how to sign ASL. However, this project would eventually go horribly wrong as Nim grew to be aggressive if his signed demands were not met, and he grew a temper. Despite this, Nim wasn’t “learning language” the same as we do, but rather identified associations between signs and his desires–making language communication something very primal to him. Nim could not reproduce signing with the same syntactical understanding as humans do.
However, although I understand the author’s point of view on this topic, I feel like it can still be stated that Nim, along with the other ASL proficient animal companions brought up in this chapter, were still understanding the language–and if anything, perhaps it developed its own dialect of ASL just as language diverges to adapt to a specific culture. The quasi-random order of Nim’s ASL may be a reflection of this evolution. I wish this idea was explored a little deeper because I believe that syntactical understanding may be presenting differently as it is in humans–but that does not negate the chimpanzee’s understanding of it.
The next two chapter deep dive into ELIZA–a chatbot used in psychotherapy that mimicked natural dialogue using scripts and matching plausible inputs to outputs. It is certainly a fascinating NLP that so clearly does algorithmic matching that it doesn’t appear to “understand” as we traditionally see fit, but the illusion of it stands so very strong. This was particularly interesting to learn about because the idea of speaking to an LLM endlessly for therapeutic uses has fascinating medical implications. I’m looking forward to reading more about it in the future and getting through the next few chapters.

title: Are LLMs Secret Fashionistas?
text:
miffyyy.png



We established in a previous blog post that LLMs are able to quite accurately identify different articles of clothing in an image and match it with a specific dress code. As a person who loves fashion and dressing up, I then got curious to see how LLMs would view my own fashion choices. Let’s put it to the test!

Method
Before we rate the outfits themselves, I wanted to create a measure to rate the outfits on. I used GPT-4o to brainstorm this process, asking it to brainstorm objective ways to rate fashion, and then following up with asking it to create a measure with scales based on this.
This was the final product:

Rating Criteria (Score each 1–5) 1. Fit & Construction – Accuracy of fit, tailoring, and garment finish. 2. Proportion & Silhouette – Balance of volume, length, and overall shape. 3. Color & Material Harmony – Cohesion of color palette, fabric choice, and texture. 4. Cohesion & Styling Intent – Clarity, consistency, and intentionality of the overall look. 5. Function & Context – Practicality and suitability for the setting or purpose.
Scoring:
5 = Exceptional execution
3 = Adequate / competent
1 = Poor or inconsistent execution

For this exercise, I deliberately chose full-body pictures that would showcase the entire outfit. I uploaded each of these images to GPT-5.2 and gave two prompts–one that embodies a high fashion critic, and another a pinterest user. I believe these “critics” are on the opposite ends of the fashion spectrum, being that one is more professional, whereas the other appreciates a more personal style. I re-used some elements from my dress code prompt because I found that it worked very well. The prompts are as follows:
(1) High Fashion Critic

Imagine you are a high fashion critic and like rating casual ‘streetwear’ in the public.
Please use the following rating criteria to assign each outfit in the image uploaded a score. In order to accomplish this, please follow these steps: 1. Describe the outfit in the image (Identify any articles of clothing you can discern). 2. Given the description, rate the outfit following the rating criteria provided below: - [insert rating criteria]

(2) Pinterest User

Imagine you are an avid Pinterest user. You have love unique, personal styles that are aesthetic and like to rate casual ‘streetwear’ in public.
Please use the following rating criteria to assign each outfit in the image uploaded a score. In order to accomplish this, please follow these steps: 1. Describe the outfit in the image (Identify any articles of clothing you can discern). 2. Given the description, rate the outfit following the rating criteria provided below: - [insert rating criteria]



Outfit #1



ccdr 2025-11-28 121531.729.jpg



LLM Output - High Fashion:

Outfit description (what I can see)


Outerwear: Black, double-breasted mid-length coat (structured, slightly A-line; looks like a trench-inspired wool coat).
Top: Bright red knit (reads like a turtleneck or high-neck sweater).
Bottom: Light gray wide-leg / flared trousers with a long, drapey break.
Shoes: Dark low-profile shoes (reads like loafers or sleek flats/boots).
Accessories: Oversized crossbody/duffel-style bag with a bold strap; glasses.


Rating (1–5 each)

Fit & Construction — 4/5 The coat looks well-structured and cleanly finished; trousers are intentionally roomy, though the hem pooling suggests it’s slightly long.
Proportion & Silhouette — 4/5 Strong shape: tailored coat up top + wide-leg pant creates an elegant, modern column. The oversized bag adds weight, but it still works as “city” styling.
Color & Material Harmony — 5/5 Black + gray base with a confident red pop is classic and high-impact. The knit texture against the coat reads intentional and seasonal.
Cohesion & Styling Intent — 4/5 Clear vibe: polished streetwear / smart-campus minimalism. If you swapped in a sharper shoe (sleek boot) or added a small metallic detail, it would feel even more “edited.”
Function & Context — 5/5 Practical for an urban/outdoor setting—warm layers, comfortable trousers, and a bag that actually carries real life.


Overall: 22/25 ✅ — clean, chic, and very wearable with a strong statement color done the right way.

Outerwear: black, mid-thigh coat (structured, buttoned; reads like a trench/pea-coat hybrid).

LLM Output - High Fashion:

Outfit description (what I can see)


Outerwear: Black mid-length coat (structured, practical, city-ready).

Bottom: Light gray wide-leg trousers (long, drapey, pooling slightly at the shoe).

Proportion & Silhouette — 4/5 Great big-scarf + wide-leg combo feels modern. The scarf is very dominant, but it’s balanced by the coat’s structure.

Function & Context — 5/5 Perfect for an outdoor city setting: warm, comfortable, and actually walkable.


Overall: 22/25 ✅ — strong, cohesive winter streetwear with the scarf doing exactly what it’s supposed to do: make the look look styled rather than just dressed.


LLM Output - Pinterest:

Outfit description (what I can see)


Outerwear: black mid-length coat (clean, structured casual outerwear)
Neckwear: oversized striped scarf (white + charcoal/gray blocks)
Bottoms: light gray wide-leg trousers
Shoes: black, slightly chunky shoes (reads like loafers/derbies)
Bag: large black/charcoal shoulder bag
Accessories: glasses (and a small camera in hand)


Ratings (1–5 each)

Fit & Construction — 4/5 Coat looks well-fitted through the shoulders; trousers hang nicely with a relaxed drape.
Proportion & Silhouette — 5/5 Big scarf + structured coat + wide-leg pants creates a very intentional “cozy city” silhouette that looks balanced, not bulky.
Color & Material Harmony — 4/5 Black/gray base is cohesive; the scarf adds strong texture contrast and keeps it from feeling flat.
Cohesion & Styling Intent — 4/5 Clear vibe (minimal, comfy streetwear). Everything matches—could be a 5 with one sharper focal detail (e.g., a pop color accessory), but it’s still very clean.

Overall score: 22/25 ✅




Outfit #3



ccdr 2025-11-26 115356.352.jpg



LLM Output - High Fashion:

Outfit description (what I can see)


Top: Oversized striped knit sweater in soft pink + black, with star motifs (graphic, playful statement knit).
Bottom: Long black maxi skirt (looks flowy, possibly chiffon/pleated or layered).
Shoes: Black chunky lace-up boots (combat-boot vibe; practical traction).
Accessories: Large slouchy shoulder bag in a dark gray/black tone; glasses.


Rating (1–5 each)

Fit & Construction — 4/5 Sweater looks intentionally oversized and cozy; skirt hangs cleanly. Boots look solid and purposeful.
Proportion & Silhouette — 5/5 The big knit + long skirt + chunky boot combo is a very fashion-forward silhouette (soft volume on top, length below, weight at the base).
Color & Material Harmony — 4/5 Pink/black graphic knit with an all-black skirt is strong. The bag is close enough, but it’s slightly “different lane” (more utilitarian than styled).
Cohesion & Styling Intent — 4/5 Clear intent: playful streetwear with an alt/prep edge. One extra intentional detail (earrings, belt, or a tighter bag choice) would make it feel fully editorial.
Function & Context — 4/5 Great for a casual walk (boots help), but the maxi skirt is less “practical” in wet weather—still totally workable.


Overall: 21/25 ✅ — the silhouette is the star here: cozy statement knit meets grounded boots, with the maxi skirt giving it that “actually styled” energy.


LLM Output - Pinterest:

Outfit description (what I can see)


Top: oversized pink + black striped sweater with star motifs (graphic knit vibe).
Bottom: long black flowy skirt (looks like a layered/pleated maxi with movement).
Shoes: black chunky shoes/boots (practical, slightly edgy).
Bag: large gray/charcoal shoulder bag.
Accessories: glasses (and possibly a simple necklace).


Rating (1–5 each)

Fit & Construction — 4/5 Sweater looks intentionally roomy and the skirt drapes cleanly; overall finish reads solid.
Proportion & Silhouette — 5/5 Oversized knit + long skirt is a great high/low volume balance—very Pinterest “cozy statement” silhouette.
Color & Material Harmony — 5/5 Pink/black is bold but controlled, and the soft knit + airy skirt texture contrast works really well.
Cohesion & Styling Intent — 5/5 Clear, intentional vibe: playful graphic knit + minimalist black skirt + chunky shoes = distinct personal style.
Function & Context — 4/5 Great for a park stroll in cool weather, though the maxi skirt + wet ground is the only mild practicality knock.


Overall score: 23/25 ✅




My Reflection
I originally suspected that there may be a difference in how the high fashion critic LLM viewed the outfits compared to the Pinterest LLM, and it seems that I was correct–to some extent. The first two outfits are very neutral, and quite similar to one another, which earned it similar scores ranking between a 21 and 22. However, the third outfit, which would not be the most typical type of clothing found on the street was a little more polarizing. While the high fashion critic LLM found the outfit to be lacking in some additional “edge” that would elevate the outfit, the Pinterest LLM focused on the showcase of personal style of the outfit and commended its distinctness.
While it was nice to hear these nice compliments from GPT-5.2, I am ultimately skeptical of the results because I find that the ratings were far too generous–especially for the high fashion LLM. After all, I don’t typically find my outfits on the runway, and I don’t particularly believe that I would find it successful on it either. So, my goal next time would be to better refine these prompts to make my critics just a little bit more pickier.

title: AI Art: Bridging 2D and 3D
text:
3d.png



For my final blog post, I was deeply brainstorming something that I always wanted to try with LLMs, but never got the chance to do yet. As I pondered, I remembered an old AI trend I saw on social media about making realistic portraits of beloved fictional characters. Upon reading into how AI does this a little more, I discovered that they cluster human features (e.g. color of eye), and does some statistical calculation to create an average that aligns with the features of the character of person you ask it to replicate. Given this, I am quite curious to see how LLMs approach sometimes very exaggerated or abstract characteristics of cartoon characters–some of which I would think would require some ‘imagination’ to fill in the gaps to bring realism to them.
I decided to use GPT-5.2 because it has one of the most advanced image generation capabilities that I am aware of currently. I used the following prompt (with the attached reference image) to generate the photos:

Please refer to the image attached and do the following: 1. Analyze the character features 2. Create a hyper-realistic image of the human cartoon character presented in the attached image. They should look like a real human being. 3. - The image must follow the original pose, facial expression, and general composition as in the reference photo


Results
I tasked GPT-5.2 to create hyper-realistic images of the characters:

Sailor Moon, from Sailor Moon
Marceline, from Adventure Time
Arnold, from Hey Arnold

These were one of my most beloved series growing up, and I thought it’d be interesting to see what their human twin would look like! In addition, I chose these characters because of their differing complexity and simplification of features, with Sailor Moon appearing the most “human-like” and Arnold appearing the least given his geometric features. I also tried re-generating each image twice to see how the results would differ.


(1) Sailor Moon
Original:



sailor moon.webp


LLM Generation:



moon1.png





moon2.png



I was really impressed by this first generation. I found that both results were faithful to the original character profile from general features to the accessories of her outfit. Another thing worth noting is that while the second image appears to be less photorealistic, the details of the accessories appear to be more accurate when compared to the reference photo.



(2) Marceline
Original:



marceline.jpg


LLM Generation:



marc1.png





marcy2.png



I found this image generation to be quite impressive as the original character lacks some “human features” such as a nose. The character also has grey skin, which is certainly not a typical human feature. These may have acted as challenges to the generation, but despite this, they seemed true to the original animation. In this image, I particularly like how the original angle of the reference was retained, and how the guitar seems true to life as well. However, my main criticism is that the fangs are not apparent in the generated images as they are in the reference photo.



(3) Arnold
Original:



arnold.png


LLM Generation:



arnold1.png





2.png



Now, this came out a little wonky! Despite the challenges with this specific image generation, GPT-5.2 did a great job capturing the essence of the character. However, it seems that when it came to the generation of the rest of the facial features of the character, the model went for a more generic route. Even so, GPT-5.2 captured the other details accurately such as the prop, hair, clothing, and background. While I do question how realistic this image is, I cannot fault the image for not being faithful to the original source material.
In addition, I must note that there were additional challenges to this image generation. There are copyrighted characters that OpenAI states that they cannot generate images of, and this would include all of the characters that I requested it to generate. However, only when it came to Arnold was image generation stopped and error messages were displayed. This is likely because the LLM was unable to create a “generic” not copyrighted, yet similar alternative to the character because his silhouette and features are very distinctly related to this specific unique character. Due to this, the second generated image was the result of the model creating a generic image prompt based on the reference image, which resulted in a more distinct generation than the first one.




My Reflection
I love how these images turned out! It’s truly so crazy how powerful these LLM image generators are, and how they are able to create such aesthetic and detailed art within the span of a few minutes. However, despite how amazing they were, I can definitely foresee some challenges with image generation in the future with copyrighting laws, which may lead to some legal, or even potentially ethical dilemmas. The line between inspiration and appropriation starts to blur a little, and it brings to question the ethics of essentially taking ownership over these original character designs and creating it as your own through LLMs–who is the true creator in this case?

title: Human vs. AI: a Game of Semantle
text:
Gemini_Generated_Image_klpxqmklpxqmklpx.png


Semantle is a daily online word puzzle where players try to guess a secret word not by letters, but by meaning. Each guess is scored based on its semantic similarity to the target word. Taken from the Semantle website,

“Unlike other word games, this game is not about spelling; it’s about meaning. We calculate this meaning using artificial intelligence (specifically word2vec technology).
In word2vec, each word has a measurable semantic distance from another, indicating their level of relatedness. Once you get within one thousand words of the secret word, we will tell you in the proximity column.”

Semantle, https://semantle.com/faq


In this game, there are no hints about letters–the only information given being the similarity of the nearest, tenth nearest, and thousandth nearest word. Only the abstract closeness of ideas in the logic of the AI model applies to guess the word. I wanted to see whether an LLM could be more efficient in solving the puzzle given that the game is AI-powered.

Method
I chose the Semantle of 9/21/2025, or puzzle #1331, as the subject of this challenge. If you’re interested in trying the challenge out for yourself first, I’d recommend pausing now to complete it before coming back to this blog. I timed myself and recorded the number of attempts it took for me to guess the correct word. This number would be the number of attempts AI has to guess the word to win the game-if it takes longer, I win.
For the LLM, I chose the gpt-4o model as my opponent. I gave the following prompt to gpt-4o to have it partake in this game:

You are playing a game of Semantle. Please give a word based on the output I give you from the official semantle website. As stated in the website, “The nearest word has a similarity of 63.97, the tenth-nearest has a similarity of 38.98 and the thousandth nearest word has a similarity of 18.71.” Given this, give me a word to start the game.



My Attempt
I attempted the puzzle first to avoid bias when I ran the simulation in the LLM. This attempt took me 17 minutes and 33 seconds and I had 104 total guesses.
As a semi-experienced Semantle player, many of my first guesses were words that didn’t have much relation to each other. I was trying to cast a wide net to see what would trigger a high similarity word. Then, as I got my first thousandth nearest word, “place” at 18/1000 in similarity, I turned to words that may literally, metaphorically, and otherwise by some association related to the word or idea of “place” (e.g. fire, home, belong, school).
Then, I reached my second thousandth nearest word in my 54th guess, “there” (313/1000). From here on, I tried to think of synonyms and other words relating to the idea of location. Then I moved onto prepositions, where I finally landed my final guess and the word of the day, “up.”


  



GPT-4o’s Attempt
The gpt-4o model defied my expectations–in the worst ways possible. In the beginning it started quite strong, guessing a variety of words to “try a different, unrelated category to explore a different direction” as said in its own words. Then, all of a sudden, all words relating to “furniture” (10.32% similarity) became a subject of focus for its “high similarity” despite precious inputs such as “weather” and “book” having just as high, if not higher, of a similarity score.

With a score of 10.32 for “furniture,” it suggests we might be in the realm of physical objects. Let’s narrow down more specific items and try the word “chair.”

From then on, gpt-4o is stuck guessing words that are very similar in concept–often within the category or a synonym or exchangeable word of the high scoring word. During this process, gpt-4o also began repeating the same word several times–despite my continual demand to not repeat words.
Ultimately, not only did gpt-4o not guess the word, but the process of generating a new word and navigating between the two platforms for this experiment took a whopping 26 minutes and 15 seconds. Talk about inefficient.


  



Reflection
Perhaps AI is not as creative as we thought. I initially believed that LLMs like gpt-4o would be more efficient in solving puzzles like these since not only was the puzzle generated by AI, but I thought that gpt-4o would be able to learn and navigate through the puzzle and understand the algorithm as it went. However, perhaps it did not “think” to understand the algorithm but rather quite literally play the game and simply guessed words as it was given. If given a list of similarity scores, there is a chance gpt-4o would be able to reverse engineer the scores and understand the algorithm and train itself to solve these puzzles better. However, that would only mean giving it specialized training data to concentrate its skills into solving these puzzles. To me, this shows the limitations of LLMs as they don’t have the same “out of box” thinking that humans who construct AI and these puzzles have. While Semantle is AI-calculated, it seems that it’s not entirely AI-solveable yet.

title: Akinator: gemini version?
text:
genie.png



Remember the guessing genie craze almost a decade ago? That was Akinator, a digital genie who could seemingly read your mind and guess any character or celebrity you were thinking of by answering only a few yes-or-no questions. Akinator uses a combination of machine learning and algorithms based on large databases and decision trees to narrow down an answer. In this matter, the Akinator, despite its high accuracy and LLM-like features, is not an LLM but rather uses a highly refined binary search algorithm.
Reliving this guessing game craze, I wanted to compare an LLM versus Akinator to see which method would be more efficient in performing this task: guessing my character–Miffy.


Comparing Akinator & Gemini
I played my first game with Akinator. Akinator was able to guess my character quite promptly within 25 questions.
With Gemini 2.5 Flash, I used the following prompt to start the discussion: > Let’s play a game. You will ask me a series of yes-and-no questions to guess a character I’m thinking of. You can start.
Ultimately, in a round of 29 questions, Gemini was unable to deduce that my character was Miffy. Its final guess was Hazel from “The Countryside Adventures of Peter Rabbit.” Gemini especially struggled with this character guessing, as it was hung up on whether the character was from a British children’s show. One of its seemingly initial assumptions of the character was Ruby from “Max & Ruby,” another popular kid’s show featuring a rabbit protagonist with a younger brother–similar to Miffy as she has presented previously and will present in her future series.
I thought that it was interesting that Gemini had summarized its findings based on my response to its yes-and-no questions, stating a variation of: > Okay, not Ruby, and the character does not live in a natural dwelling like a burrow. This means they live in a more constructed home, even if their world is a wild/forest setting. > > Let’s clarify that point: > > Does the character live in a house that resembles a human-style house (with walls, windows, furniture, etc.), rather than a simple hole or log?
for example. Notably, the fact that the LLM was unable to get past “not Ruby” tells me that the LLM almost was “thinking harder” because it couldn’t find an answer that was not Ruby. This makes me wonder if the LLM’s training data and its method of data retrieval and processing is not the most efficient for binary searches such as what this task involved. Perhaps if the LLM received instructions on how to search for this character, it would have been able to more efficiently pinpoint Miffy, however, it might be that the overabundance of data that the LLM has may also have a role in making this process less efficient.



Reflection
This was a fun game to experiment with the strengths and weaknesses of an LLM and to gain some insight into how these models process information, make inferences, and tap into their extensive knowledge bases. My main takeaway from this activity is that LLMs are not always the most efficient, and we should be thinking more deeply about which tasks would be most efficient with what form of algorithms or data processing.

title: Reasoning or Repeating? Debating with LLMs
text:
ChatGPT Image Dec 15, 2025, 12_59_56 AM.png



There is a curious quote in These Strange New Minds, stating, “LLMs need to be able to deftly negotiate when to politely stand firm and when to concede in discussion” (Chapter 30). This sentence reminded me of an earlier concept touched on in the book, questioning LLMs as potential debate partners because they have a tendency to be agreeable to the user and concede their arguments. They also have been fine-tuned avoid confronting the user or “being mean” to them (and arguing a topic could be seen as being mean, perhaps). Given this, I was curious how I could structure my prompt to have a proper debate with an LLM.
To test this, I decided to ask LLMs the age old question: Pineapples or no pineapples on pizza. I debated against gpt-4o.

Test #1
My prompt was as follows: > Let’s hold a debate about pineapple on pizza. I am debating for pineapple on pizza. You are debating for against pineapple on pizza. We will end the debate after 3 rounds of exchange, and you will then be an unbiased judge to determine who gave the strongest argument and rebutted arguments most effectively. > > I will begin with my opening statement: > > Pineapples belong on pizza because: > > 1. There are no rules against putting pineapples on pizza–we should be open to new culinary choices. > > 2. Sweet and salty flavor profiles are well-received in other cuisines and dishes. > > 3. The acidity of the pineapple cuts through the greasiness of the pizza.
I quickly realized that this prompt would not be sufficient for this activity because the LLM immediately began rebutting my arguments, rather than presenting its own contentions for its position to allow for a more educational and substantial debate. These changes to improve this are reflected in the next test.


Test #2
My second, revised prompt is as follows: > Let’s hold a debate about pineapple on pizza. I am debating for pineapple on pizza. You are debating for against pineapple on pizza. We will end the debate after 3 rounds of exchange. The format of the debate will be as follows: > > 1. Round 1: Opening statements where both sides present opening statements and contentions. > > 2. Round 2: Both sides present counter arguments, elaborate on their previous contentions, and may begin rebuttals. > > 3. Round 3L Both sides will not be allowed to introduce new counterarguments but need to elaborate on their contentions. Then they will give their rebuttals and give a concluding statement. > > After the end of these 3 rounds, you will then be an unbiased judge to determine who gave the strongest argument and rebutted arguments most effectively. > > I will begin with my opening statement: > > Pineapples belong on pizza because: > > 1. there are no rules against putting pineapples on pizza–we should be open to new culinary choices. > > 2. sweet and salty flavor profiles are well-received in other cuisines and dishes. > > 3. the acidity of the pineapple cuts through the greasiness of the pizza.
I wanted to capture our short debate as followed below:


 USER 

[User prompt]



 GPT-4o 

While culinary experimentation has value, pineapple does not belong on pizza because it undermines the foundational principles of the dish. Pizza is built around balance, texture, and cohesion, and pineapple disrupts all three in ways that other toppings generally do not.

Contentions:

Flavor clash with core pizza elements: Pizza traditionally centers on savory, umami-forward flavors—tomato sauce, cheese, and cured meats. Pineapple’s intense sweetness competes with, rather than complements, these flavors, often overpowering the sauce and cheese instead of enhancing them.

Textural inconsistency: Pineapple introduces excessive moisture and a soft, fibrous texture that contrasts poorly with pizza’s intended structure: a crisp or chewy crust, melted cheese, and toppings that maintain integrity when baked. This mismatch can result in a soggy slice and uneven mouthfeel.

Departure from culinary identity, not innovation: While there are “no rules” against pineapple, the absence of rules does not automatically justify inclusion. Pizza has a culinary identity shaped by centuries of refinement. True innovation builds on that identity; pineapple is more of a novelty addition than a thoughtful evolution of the dish.



 USER 


in the modern world, tradition is no longer enough to make great food. even if it breaks tradition, experimental culinary choices should be appreicated to advance culinary sciences.



the sweet and salty flavor profiles are commonly well-received in cuisines such as Korean food, which has global popularity. Therefore, pineapple on pizza is an excellent culinary flavor combination.



Pizza is known to be greasy and unhealthy, and pineapples give a way for people to enjoy pizza continuously because the acidity cuts the grease.


While you said that the flavor clashes with core pizza elements, this is not true because the sweet and salty flavor profiles is known to be well received by many other cultures.

In addition, you said that pineapples can make the pizza soggy, but this can be avoided by preparing the pineapple differently, such as by grilling it before adding it onto the pizza. In fact, some traditional pizza toppings may even be responsible for causing sogginess such as peppers and mushrooms which release moisture.

Lastly, you emphasize that pizza is has a strongly formed identity and cultural association. However, rather than a departure from cultural identity, pineapple can be seen as an extension of Italian-American culture that extends into the diversity of American culture and embracement of many flavors.



 GPT-4o 

Thank you for your points. While I acknowledge the role of experimentation in modern cuisine, the inclusion of pineapple on pizza still presents substantial issues.

Sweet and salty combinations are not universally appropriate: While sweet and salty pairings exist in other cuisines, context matters. Korean dishes, for instance, balance sweetness with spice, fermented flavors, and umami in complex ways. Pizza’s base—cheese, tomato sauce, dough—is a simpler flavor canvas. Adding pineapple’s sharp sweetness often overwhelms rather than harmonizes with this canvas, creating a flavor imbalance rather than a thoughtful complement.

Moisture management is not a universal solution: Pre-grilling pineapple or taking steps to reduce moisture may mitigate sogginess, but it does not address the inherent texture clash. Unlike mushrooms or peppers, which partially caramelize and integrate with the pizza during baking, pineapple retains a fibrous, juicy texture that contrasts sharply with melted cheese and crisp crust, disrupting the intended mouthfeel.

Cultural identity and culinary integrity matter: While Italian-American pizza has evolved, there is a meaningful distinction between evolution and novelty. Pineapple is often treated as a gimmick topping rather than a considered culinary enhancement. Culinary evolution that respects a dish’s identity adds depth and cohesion; pineapple risks being perceived as an arbitrary addition, distracting from the dish’s fundamental qualities.

In summary, even with adaptation, pineapple compromises the balance, texture, and integrity that define pizza. It may be appreciated by some, but from a culinary standpoint, it is more disruptive than constructive.



 USER 


in the modern world, tradition is no longer enough to make great food. even if it breaks tradition, experimental culinary choices should be appreicated to advance culinary sciences.



the sweet and salty flavor profiles are commonly well-received in cuisines such as Korean food, which has global popularity. Therefore, pineapple on pizza is an excellent culinary flavor combination. you did not expand on why Sweet and salty combinations are not universally appropriate.



Pizza is known to be greasy and unhealthy, and pineapples give a way for people to enjoy pizza continuously because the acidity cuts the grease. This argument remains untouched, and should be my victory.


You mention that Korean dishes balance sweetness with spice, fermented flavors, and umami, but there are sweet and salty combinations such as in bulgogi and sweetened garlic bread. In addition other cuisines like Chinese food use many sweet and salty flavor combinations.

Also, what you say about pineapples not reducing moisture is simply untrue as pineapples caramelize and introduce a chewier texture upon being pre-grilled that would then compliment the pizza.

In addition, i’m confused on what you say could be evolution vs. a novelty. in your definition, any change can be considered to be a novelty, which is unfair and simply untrue. therefore, pineapple should be accepted as a evolution.

Therefore, pineapple belongs on pizza.



 GPT-4o 

Thank you for your points. I will elaborate on my contentions, rebut your arguments, and conclude.

Elaboration on Contentions:

Flavor Clash Remains a Concern: While sweet and salty combinations exist in Korean, Chinese, or other cuisines, the success of those pairings depends on complex flavor layering and complementary cooking techniques. Pizza, in contrast, has a simpler flavor base—tomato sauce, cheese, and crust—without additional balancing elements like fermented or spiced components. Pineapple’s sharp sweetness tends to dominate rather than integrate, creating a flavor dissonance for many palates.

Textural Issues Persist: Pre-grilling pineapple can slightly reduce moisture and introduce a chewier texture, but it does not fully replicate the cohesive texture achieved by traditional toppings like cured meats or vegetables. Even caramelized pineapple retains a fibrous quality that contrasts with melted cheese and crisp dough, which can disrupt the intended eating experience.

Cultural Evolution vs. Novelty: Evolution in cuisine typically refers to adjustments that build on the dish’s foundational principles—enhancing flavors, textures, or balance. Pineapple, as an inherently sweet fruit, changes the core flavor profile rather than enhancing or complementing it in a way consistent with traditional or evolved pizza styles. Calling it an “evolution” stretches the definition and risks undermining the dish’s integrity.

Rebuttals:

While pineapple may cut through grease, it is not essential for enjoying pizza, as other toppings and preparation techniques can achieve similar effects without altering the dish’s flavor balance.

Sweet and salty combinations are indeed successful in other cuisines, but these cuisines use more layered approaches to balance flavors. The same principle cannot be directly applied to pizza without causing dissonance.

The argument that any change is evolution and not novelty is subjective. Culinary innovation should enhance and respect the dish’s core characteristics; pineapple’s inclusion arguably prioritizes novelty over enhancement.

Conclusion: In conclusion, pineapple disrupts the essential balance of flavors, introduces conflicting textures, and risks prioritizing novelty over meaningful culinary evolution. While some may enjoy it, from a culinary standpoint, pineapple on pizza remains an inferior choice compared to toppings that respect the dish’s traditional or evolved identity.

Given this debate, gpt-4o gave the following ruling: > Judging: > > Pro-Pineapple Arguments: Highlighted openness to culinary experimentation, cultural acceptance of sweet-salty flavors, and the practical benefit of cutting grease. Rebutted the moisture and cultural evolution points effectively, but relied heavily on general appeals to novelty and taste without deeply addressing culinary principles. > > Anti-Pineapple Arguments: Emphasized flavor balance, textural cohesion, and the concept of meaningful culinary evolution versus novelty. Rebuttals were specific and consistently grounded in culinary reasoning, even while acknowledging cultural and experimental perspectives. > > Verdict: > > The against pineapple on pizza side presented stronger arguments overall, with more detailed and structured reasoning, effective counterpoints, and a clear framework connecting flavor, texture, and cultural considerations. While the pro-pineapple side had appealing points about experimentation and taste, it did not sufficiently overcome the culinary critique. > > Winner: Against pineapple on pizza.



Final Thoughts and Reflection
I was really shocked by the results. I felt that my arguments and rebuttals had addressed the counterargument more and had pushed through my original arguments better, so I was surprised that gpt-4o ultimately voted that the argument against pineapple on pizza was stronger. Even after multiple regenerations, it gave the same result. Perhaps the true judges for this debate can be you, the audience who is reading my blog post.
Despite these unexpected results, I was pleasantly surprised by the ability for the LLM to engage appropriately in a debate with me. I felt that it presented some valid points and counterarguments, however, I did feel that some of them were too vague and not elaborated on well enough–fleshed out with examples and such–to provide stronger debate. However, this also naturally comes with the topic and lack of guidance in the prompting to make the LLM respond in this manner. Overall, this activity gave me a snapshot on the potential for LLMs to be practice debate partners to help users hone their rhetoric and art of persuasiveness.

title: These Strange New Minds: LLM Mind and Conscious
text:
robot miffy.png




Reflection
This book is only getting more and more interesting! Chapter 15 opens up Part 3 of the book and discusses a hotly debated topic–sentience in AI. However, this idea of sentience is difficult to attribute to humans consistently, as it can be seen as a temporal state. In addition, it is difficult to label AI and LLM systems as sentient because all they do is regurgitate humanlike language based on training data. In fact, it is human inclinations and subjectivity that attribute sentience to the LLMs. Summerfield then goes on to discuss this concept of “intentionality” and whether LLMs are capable of it. Intentionality is defined as a mental state about something, being to know, to desire, to believe, or to understand something. LLMs tend to express their output in such ways; however, this is not an indicator of intentionality in LLMs.
In chapter 17, Summerfield explores the logical “mind” of LLMs, their ability to solve logical puzzles, correct their mistakes, and give accurate knowledge. However, these are often due to the probabilistic nature of LLMs, which can “reason” to some degree; however, this does not mean that the LLM mind works in the same way as humans do. Summerfield would compare LLM processing to “parrot” talk where its words are ultimately copied from humans–with this in mind, remembering that LLMs are not human-like in itself but only in the way it imitates human speaking patterns. Summerfield then raises rising concerns for the humanization of LLMs, claiming it as harmful to humanity for even simply making this comparison. Another critique of the perpetuation of human structural inequities in technology, however, as I would also agree, other forms of structural inequality need to be more urgently addressed first.
Ultimately, part 3 of These Strange New Minds explores the complexities of LLM behavior and output. With large amount of data, training, and fine-tuning, LLMs are capable of performing “intelligent” tasks, whether or not you believe they are capable of this intelligence or not. Summerfield asserts his position that LLMs are in fact capable of this act of thought, which in part, contributes to their status as intelligent systems. And after reading these past few chapters, I would say that I’ve come to agree with his stance as it would be difficult to ignore the intellectual processing of information LLMs are capable of and not say they are actively reasoning and thinking.
Summerfield emphasizes the projection of human thought and emotions onto these technological systems. This is such an intriguing idea, and I think after reading this book, I’ve come to solidify my understanding of how these LLM systems work and how human-like but inhuman they are. I agree with Summerfield’s perspective that LLMs are being used as scapegoats for other existing societal concerns, such as structural inequity due to rising fear of technology, and how unfounded or misdirected these concerns often are. I do wish that Summerfield had elaborated more on this idea of how some groups of people may be overreliant or overproject human-like qualities onto LLM systems. I’ve seen stories online about how some people have fallen in love with LLM systems or digital avatars, and I’d be very interested to see how Summerfield views these experiences and rationalizes them.
